chapter_theme: The opening of Thirikona Siddhar's kalivenba, a single run-on poem of praise: Siva is the supreme guru, the one form in which Vishnu, Brahma and Rudra shone, the great faith that sees no difference among the disputing sects, the one who is beginning, middle and end, who became the three gunas, the senses and the three impurities, who is the five, eight and fifty-one letters and the pranava, who walks at the root beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the sushumna, and who, false to the false and true to the true, takes a guru's form to free his old servants.
structure_note: The whole work (2145 to 2234) is one kalivenba; each unit here is a two-line slice whose last word begins the next unit's clause, so readings are of the sense that runs across the cut. 2145 to 2149 invoke Siva as guru and as the one behind the Trinity and the sects; 2150 to 2156 are his epithets as Lord of the cosmos; 2157 to 2169 describe him as the one who takes every quality, letter and form, who is beyond the channels and beyond description, and who descends as guru. The epithets continue into chapter 111.

2145.reading: Siva alone is the supreme guru, the preceptor; his feet alone, every day, are what one holds to; and he is the one behind Vishnu, whose epithet the run-on line begins.
2145.nuance: The unit ends in நவநீத, which belongs to the next unit (the butter-stealing, cloud-coloured Vishnu). The first line sets the theme of the whole poem: the guru is Siva, and Siva comes as guru (2168 to 2170).

2146.reading: The blue cloud-coloured one who blossomed gold (Vishnu of the fresh butter), the four-faced one who flashed lightning from his sensing mouth, Brahma the Veda-lord, and the red-matted one of the south: all three are named as the forms of the one Lord of 2147.
2146.nuance: பொறிவாய் மின்பூத்த is obscure; it may describe Brahma's mouths as sparking with the Veda. நான்முகனும் வேதாவும் may name one god twice or Brahma and a separate Veda-lord. தென்பூத்த carries into 2147 to qualify the red-haired Rudra.

2147.reading: The red-matted one too: the Lord arose alone, as the one form in which all these shone with lustre; and he is the great faith (2148) that argues no Vedas.
2147.nuance: ஒக்கத் தனிவந்து உதித்த: the Trinity are not three gods but one Lord who rose alone bearing all their lustre. தர்க்கமிடும் carries into 2148 to qualify the Vedas and shastras as things that dispute.

2148.reading: The many sects need disputing Vedas and shastras; he is the great faith that sees no difference among them, and his sound subsides into nada (2149).
2148.nuance: பெருஞ்சமயம் is set against பலசமயம்: the one great religion against the many. The claim is not that sects are false but that difference (பேதம்) is not seen from the great one. 2151 names the attitude சமரசம்.

2149.reading: He is the one who experiences, with sound subsiding into nada and desire subsiding in the house of the light-space; and his feet rest in the heart of devotees who worship (2150).
2149.nuance: ஒளியம்பரமனையில் I read as ஒளி அம்பர மனையில், the house that is the space of light; tradition takes such space as the inner expanse of awareness. அனுபவிப்போன் makes God the experiencer, a Siddhar turn: the state the yogi reaches is what God already is.

2150.reading: His soft feet are the fragrant lotus that took root and opened in the petals of the heart-spring of servants who worship; and he appears in all eight directions (2151).
2150.nuance: The heart is a spring (சுனை) in which the Lord's foot-lotus blooms; the image makes worship the water, not the offering. எண்டிக்கும் carries into 2151.

2151.reading: Appearing as every kind in the eight directions, he stays as concord; he does not divide, and his simplicity has no guile; he is the first (2152).
2151.nuance: சாதியான் can mean one who appears as every species or as every caste; either way the next word, சமரசம், makes him the harmony among them. பேதமையான் is odd praise, since பேதைமை is folly; here it seems to mean guileless simplicity, as the following வஞ்சம் இலா suggests. ஆதி carries into 2152.

2152.reading: He is the beginning as first, middle and end, and ending them, he is the light of the open void; and across a hundred crore births (2153) he gives release.
2152.nuance: சிதலாய் is unclear; சிதல் is the termite, so a crumbling or scattering may be meant, as the ending of all three phases into the void-light. வெளியொளி (light of the open) is the Siddhars' name for the Lord beyond form, picked up in 2168.

2153.reading: Through a hundred crore births, meditating Shakti and mantra as himself, the whole First One gives release; and his red matted hair is wound up (2154).
2153.nuance: Who meditates is ambiguous: the Lord who holds Shakti and mantra as himself, or the soul who through many births comes to meditate them as itself and is given release. சுத்திய carries into 2154 to describe the wound red hair.

2154.reading: He of the wound red hair does not enter the hearts of those who, though they have mastered the state of yoga, do not aim at him; he wears the young moon and his throat holds poison (2155).
2154.nuance: The verse separates yoga from devotion: yogic attainment without taking the Lord as the mark (குறி) leaves the heart empty of him. This qualifies the whole work's yoga teaching in 2188 to 2194.

2155.reading: Poison-throated, a vision hard to seek, Lord of many crore eggs, light that is formless and formed; and he loves the red lotus (2156).
2155.nuance: அருவுருவான் (formless-formed) is the Siddhanta middle term between form and formlessness, taken up in 2168 where he is beyond both.

2156.reading: Loving the red lotus-bud, the sea and the mountain, he is the one whose three acts are a play; and he is the Siva-siddha (2157) whose word makes things known.
2156.nuance: மூன்று தொழில் is three acts, not the Siddhanta five; creation, keeping and dissolving are meant. சூதுபுரி makes them a game or trick. முண்டகச் செம்போதம் is read as the red lotus bud; போதம் could also be knowledge, giving 'red knowledge'.

2157.reading: The Siva-siddha who set things so that they can be discerned by those who recite; in turiya (2158) he comes to birth as atom, mote and flame.
2157.nuance: Only one line survives for this unit (see source_issues), so the sense is carried by the words that frame it: ஓதும் from 2156 and துரியத்தில் leading into 2158. சிவசித்தன் names the Lord as the siddha.

2158.reading: In turiya he comes as atom, as dust-mote, as flame-light, firming into a form, and is born; and (2159) he becomes the gunas, senses and impurities.
2158.nuance: தோத்தி and தேத்தி are obscure; தோற்றி (appearing) and தேற்றி (firming) are the likely words. The sequence atom, mote, flame, form is a descent from the subtle to the gross, read by tradition as the Lord's own taking of embodiment. சாத்தரிய at the end is unclear (perhaps சாத்திரிய, 'of the shastras') and recurs at 2169.

2159.reading: Having become the three gunas, the five senses and the three impurities, he stays as every quality and gives grace; and he is the letters (2160).
2159.nuance: The Lord is not only beyond the gunas and malas but is them: the bonds themselves are his grace at work. This is a stronger claim than Siddhanta usually makes, where the impurities are other than Pati.

2160.reading: He is the five letters, the eight letters, the fifty-one letters, the tender letter, and everywhere the pranava; and he is the little meaning (2161).
2160.nuance: The five letters are Siva's mantra; the eight may be the eight-syllable mantra (ஓம் நமசிவாய with its seed syllables); the fifty-one are the Sanskrit alphabet as the matrika. பிஞ்செழுத்து (the tender or young letter) is unexplained; it may be the unspoken letter beyond the fifty. கொஞ்சப் carries into 2161.

2161.reading: As meaning, as delusion, as flaw, as word, as grace, the Blissful One stood alone; and his vision does not darken (2162).
2161.nuance: The list pairs opposites, meaning and delusion, flaw and grace, so that nothing is outside him; the thought matches 2159. புரையாய் (as flaw or cavity) is odd praise and may be a copying error for பொறையாய்.

2162.reading: He is unclouded vision to those who have seen, and for those who have not he stands as form and as the subtle; he is the worker, and his rule (2163) is beyond the channels.
2162.nuance: The Lord's mode depends on the seer: direct sight for the realised, form and hidden subtlety for the rest. தொழிலாளி, the worker, picks up the three acts of 2156.

2163.reading: Beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the whirl-point, he walks at the furthest root; he owns the sea and rides the bull (2164).
2163.nuance: சுழி is read as சுழிமுனை, the sushumna; the three channels are the yogi's instruments, and the Lord is said to be beyond even them, yet walking மூலக் கடையில், at the root's end, which tradition takes as the muladhara. The plain sense is that technique does not reach him; the coded sense places him at the base of the body.

2164.reading: The one of bonds who dwells in the house of Parashakti the kutilai, the One without birth or death, the yogi (2165) who cannot be described.
2164.nuance: குடிலை is the primal bent power from which nada and bindu arise, here identified with Parashakti; her house is the Lord's dwelling. பாசன் may mean the Lord of the bonds, who binds, or be a variant of பாசம்-bearer. பிறப்புறப்பு is read as birth and departure.

2165.reading: The yogi of whom none can say small or great, red or black, short or tall; and his bond is mingled with the senses (2166).
2165.nuance: The apophatic list, no size, colour or height, is the Siddhar way of refusing the icon; it belongs with 2168 and 2199. பொறிகலந்த carries into 2166.

2166.reading: He whose bond is mingled with the senses is, for those who have cut the bond, the stainless gem-light of the hall, and the loving one (2167).
2166.nuance: மாசத்தான் is read as மாசற்றான், stainless; the first spelling would say the opposite. மண்டத்தான் suggests மண்டபம், the hall, so the gem-light recalls Chidambaram, named again at 2197 and 2206.

2167.reading: To the false he is false and to the true he is truth, dwelling in each heart, standing in the open; he is the Father (2168) beyond form.
2167.nuance: The Lord answers to the quality of the seeker, as in 2162; the false find only falsehood. வெளிநின்றோன் (standing in the open) recalls the வெளியொளி of 2152.

2168.reading: The Father, the great Mayan beyond form, formlessness, light, space and seed, became guru (2169) and praised, freed his old servants.
2168.nuance: The list surpasses 2155: not formless-formed but beyond both, and beyond the light and space that the earlier units used as his names. கன மாயன் (the great Mayan) is Vishnu's epithet applied to Siva, consistent with 2147 where the Trinity is one.

2169.reading: Becoming guru, he removes the encircling deeds of the old servants who praise him, changes their form, and makes them his own; and he is the great yogi who took a human body (2170).
2169.nuance: உருமாத்தி (changing the form) is the guru's work on the disciple, which tradition reads as the transformation of the body itself and not only of the mind. சாத்தரிய recurs from 2158 and is as obscure here.

links.note: Both make the identification flatly: Tirumular says Nandi declared the guru is Siva and people do not grasp it; Thirikonar opens by naming Siva himself as the supreme guru and preceptor, and ends the chapter with Siva taking a guru's form.

Tirumular's six sects are roads to one city, and those who call one good and another bad bark like a dog at a hill; Thirikonar's Lord is the great faith that sees no difference among the sects that need disputing scriptures.

Sivavakkiyar addresses the Lord as the one who stood as ida, pingala and the sushumna themselves; Thirikonar says the Lord walks at the root beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the whirl-point. The conflict holds if 2163 denies that the channels are the Lord's modes, rather than only that they are the means of reaching him.

Both set the Lord at the root: Tirumular has the yogi take up ida and pingala and twist at the root in the triangle to see his feet; Thirikonar's Lord walks at the root's end, where the channels cannot reach him.

Both refuse every predicate of size and colour: Sivavakkiyar's cause is not great, not small, beyond black, red and white; Thirikonar's yogi cannot be called small or great, red or black, short or tall.

source_issues: 2157 (thirikonar:13) has only one line where every other unit of the kalivenba has two; a line is missing, and the sense is carried by the words that frame it.
The units are mechanical two-line slices of one continuous kalivenba, so almost every unit ends with a word that belongs grammatically to the next unit; readings follow the sense across the cut.
